**Moment one.**

"Find a way" requires knowing exactly what you are working with before proposing a solution. There are three distinct problems that must not be conflated: STING activation from c-di-GMP delivery, STING amplification from ZC3H12A KO removing the degradation brake, and reduced apoptotic tolerance from BCL2L1 downregulation in BCOR KO cells. These are three separate mechanisms converging on the same failure mode. Any fix that addresses only one of them leaves the other two intact.

---

**Moment two**, building from one.

The c-di-GMP problem is already resolved by the document — retire it, replace with doxycycline or rapamycin. That branch is closed. The remaining two problems are structural to the TIF chassis itself. ZC3H12A KO is load-bearing for the TIF phenotype — it suppresses inflammatory cytokine production, which is why it is in the design. You cannot simply restore ZC3H12A without partially dismantling what makes TIF cells viable long-term. BCL2L1 downregulation is a consequence of BCOR KO, similarly load-bearing. So the question is not "can we undo these" — the answer is no without losing the chassis. The question is: can the downstream consequences be managed without reversing the upstream knockouts.

---

**Moment three**, building from two.

There are three viable intervention categories for STING suppression in cells that cannot have ZC3H12A restored. First: cell-intrinsic STING pathway suppression via an additional genetic element — a dominant-negative STING variant, STING1 knockdown, or expression of a viral STING antagonist such as SAVI-suppressing peptides. This would make the TIF cells constitutively STING-deaf regardless of what signals reach them. Second: upstream prevention — ensure no STING-activating ligand ever reaches the cells in operating conditions, which the c-di-GMP retirement already addresses for the induction circuit, but lentiviral delivery and any future nucleic acid cargo still represent transient activation windows. Third: downstream buffering of the BCL2L1 deficit — forced expression of BCL2L1 or BCL2 under a constitutive promoter as an additional transgene, restoring apoptotic tolerance independent of BCOR KO effects. These three categories are not mutually exclusive and the severity of the ZC3H12A amplification risk may justify deploying more than one.

---

**Moment four**, building from three.

The cleanest single intervention with the highest confidence basis is dominant-negative STING or STING1 knockdown delivered as part of the initial TIF cell engineering package. STING1 knockout or knockdown in primary human T cells has published precedent — it does not eliminate T cell function, and CD8+ T cells with STING loss-of-function remain capable of effector responses through STING-independent pathways. For TIF cells, which already have effector function intentionally suppressed, the functional cost of STING silencing is lower than it would be in normal CD8+ T cells. This makes STING1 knockdown a high-fit addition to the chassis: it addresses both the ZC3H12A amplification risk and any residual innate sensing events from lentiviral delivery, and it adds one additional CRISPR target to an engineering process already performing two knockouts. The marginal cost is low. The risk reduction is structural and permanent.

---

**Moment five**, building from four.

The revised chassis would then carry three CRISPR knockouts: BCOR, ZC3H12A, and STING1. The BCL2L1 deficit from BCOR KO remains, and if the Synthesize Bio modeling of ZC3H12A KO + IFN stimulation returns a severity result significantly worse than wild-type PBMC, a BCL2L1 rescue transgene should be added as well. The recommended immediate next step is the ZC3H12A KO + IFN experiment in Synthesize Bio — that result sets the floor and determines whether STING1 knockdown alone closes the gap or whether BCL2L1 rescue is also required. The proposed alteration document should be updated to add STING1 knockdown as Change 5 in the architecture revision, with the ZC3H12A experiment as the validation gate before design lock. This is addressable. The risk is real but the mechanism is known and the intervention space is not empty.

External charging hardware is conventional: bed surfaces, recliners, and chairs incorporate transmitter coils using standard resonant inductive coupling at sub-MHz frequencies. The choice of operating frequency in the sub-MHz range is deliberate — lower frequencies penetrate tissue with reduced attenuation and produce lower SAR per unit delivered power [D3, D10]. The 6.78 MHz ISM band used in higher-frequency consumer wireless charging is also viable but produces higher local SAR for equivalent delivered power and is reserved for shorter-range high-efficiency applications.

Pelvic bone, long bones (femur, tibia, humerus), and sternal node receive the primary charging coils. The petrous bone primary node (§5.2) does not host charging coils. The wireless charging coils' tunable resonance is exploited as an MRI safety feature. Iron oxide arrays cannot detune but their heating risk is much lower than that of metallic coils. Storage components are specified in §13 in detail. #### 12.5.1 Mitochondrial Bioenergetics Foundation

Cellular ATP production in mammalian tissues occurs predominantly through oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria, with the electron transport chain (ETC) coupling electron flow from NADH and FADH2 substrates to proton pumping across the inner mitochondrial membrane [E1, E2]. The mammalian ETC comprises complexes I–IV plus the mobile electron carriers ubiquinone and cytochrome c, with electron transfer through the complexes coupled to proton translocation that establishes a transmembrane electrochemical gradient [E1]. The proton gradient, the electron flux through the ETC complexes, and the membrane potential are all directly electrical phenomena at the inner mitochondrial membrane.

The biological capacity to conduct electrons from intracellular metabolism to extracellular acceptors is established in microbial bioelectrochemistry. *Geobacter* and *Shewanella* species perform extracellular electron transfer (EET) as a metabolic strategy, conducting electrons from internal metabolic processes to external mineral or electrode acceptors through specialized cellular structures [F1, F2]. *Geobacter sulfurreducens* electrically conductive pili (e-pili) are protein filaments that serve as conductive nanowires extending from the cell surface, with characterized genetic basis and structural features [F3, F4]. *Shewanella* species use a combination of outer-membrane c-type cytochromes and conductive nanowires for similar function [F1, F4]. The proposed architectural application is the engineering of cells co-located with mitochondria-rich populations in bone marrow that express microbial EET machinery (or eukaryotic equivalents derived from cytochrome electron transfer chains) to harvest a fraction of mitochondrial electron output during up-regulated activity. The cells do not replace mitochondria; they conduct a small fraction of the surplus electron flow during periods of metabolic up-regulation to the substrate's electrical network.

# The Bio Integrase Platform™ — Addendum III
## Post-GEM Testing Architecture Revision and Wet Lab Validation Requirements

**Author:** Rickey Jay Bennett II
**ORCID:** 0009-0005-1448-9999
**Date:** June 2026
**Supersedes in part:** v3.5 §4.2 (NIR Communication Circuit induction mechanism), §18.1 (MrkH status reclassification)
**Platform DOI:** 10.5281/zenodo.20310512
**Based on:** Synthesize Bio GEM virtual experiments, June 2026 (datasets linked below)

---

## A. Scope of This Addendum

This addendum records findings from virtual gene expression modeling of the architecture's critical induction risk pathway, documents the consequent fatal flaw in the current induction design, specifies the minimum architectural revision required to resolve that flaw, and catalogues all remaining experimental questions that virtual modeling cannot resolve and that require wet lab access to advance. It is organized in three sections: (A) this scope statement, (B) the induction mechanism revision, and (C) the complete wet lab requirement register.

The GEM modeling was performed using Synthesize Bio's virtual gene expression platform. All datasets are linked at their first citation. Virtual modeling has specific limits that are acknowledged where they constrain the findings; those limits are named explicitly rather than papered over.

---

## B. Induction Mechanism Revision

### B.1 The Identified Flaw

The v3.5 architecture (§4.2) specifies c-di-GMP as the induction signal delivered to TIF cells, with MrkH as the c-di-GMP-responsive transcriptional activator driving downstream gene expression. The architecture already flagged mammalian MrkH transcriptional function as the keystone unverified component. The GEM experiments reported here establish that the problem is upstream of MrkH and is not contingent on MrkH validation — the induction signal itself is fatally incompatible with the TIF chassis regardless of whether MrkH functions as hoped.

**Experiment 1** modeled IFN-beta stimulated PBMC versus untreated control PBMC as a proxy for STING pathway activation, using c-di-GMP → STING → IRF3 → IFNB1 → downstream IFN signaling. IFN-beta at 50 ng/mL, 24 hours, 5 samples per group, bulk RNA-seq modality. Dataset: https://app.synthesize.bio/datasets/5487d0a5-5937-4ca5-be3e-876c9e62f5ad

The STING/IFN activation profile:

| Gene | log2FC | padj | Interpretation |
|------|--------|------|----------------|
| IFIT1 | +8.35 | 9.6e-119 | ISG — 322-fold upregulation |
| IFI44L | +6.87 | 9.3e-145 | ISG |
| RSAD2 (Viperin) | +6.64 | 2.3e-149 | ISG — most statistically significant gene in dataset |
| IFIT3 | +6.52 | 1.4e-103 | ISG |
| IRF7 | +6.22 | 6.8e-32 | IFN transcription factor — amplifies response |
| MX1 | +5.23 | 1.2e-95 | Canonical ISG |
| ISG15 | +5.02 | 2.9e-92 | ISG |
| OAS1 | +4.45 | 3.6e-45 | ISG / antiviral |
| CXCL10 | +3.98 | 3.6e-23 | Chemokine — recruits immune cells |
| LAG3 | +1.50 | 1.9e-07 | Early exhaustion marker — upregulated at 24h |
| TNF | -1.53 | 0.0027 | Effector function suppressed |
| NKG7 | -1.24 | 0.0009 | Cytotoxic function marker suppressed |

The interferon response is not a manageable side effect. It is the dominant transcriptional event in the entire dataset. The ISG storm is what c-di-GMP delivery continuously imposes on any cell that hosts STING — which every mammalian cell does.

**Experiment 2** modeled BCOR CRISPR KO PBMC versus normal PBMC to establish the baseline transcriptomic profile of the TIF modification without drug stimulation. 5 samples per group, bulk RNA-seq modality. Dataset: https://app.synthesize.bio/datasets/d2e5822a-e1ff-4687-b365-e1ac3c67b567

The BCOR KO baseline profile confirmed the TIF chassis is functioning as designed — effector function suppressed, exhaustion markers reduced, no constitutive innate immune activation at baseline. STING pathway components (STING1, cGAS/MB21D1, IRF3, TBK1, IRF7) and ISGs (MX1, IFIT1, ISG15, OAS1) were not significantly changed at BCOR KO baseline. The TIF chassis is not pre-inflamed. The design is working.

One critical finding emerged: BCL2L1 (Bcl-xL) is significantly downregulated in BCOR KO cells at -2.17 log2FC (padj 2.2e-11). Bcl-xL is a primary anti-apoptotic buffer in T cells. When the ISG storm from STING activation hits BCOR KO cells, those cells have reduced apoptotic protection to weather it — the TIF modification does not protect against STING, it reduces the margin against it.

**Combined vulnerability stack in TIF cells under c-di-GMP induction:**

1. c-di-GMP delivered → STING activated → ISG storm dominating the transcriptome
2. BCOR KO cells carry reduced Bcl-xL → lower apoptotic tolerance under sustained IFN
3. LAG3 starts low in BCOR KO cells but IFN-beta pushes it back up → shorter runway to exhaustion
4. Effector function already suppressed by BCOR KO → further suppression from IFN compounds functional loss
5. The gene circuit is continuous — c-di-GMP delivery is repeated, not a single bolus; chronic STING activation is the realistic operating condition

**Classification: Fatal flaw in the current induction design.** The induction signal actively degrades the cells the circuit is designed to maintain.

### B.2 Status Reclassification of MrkH

In v3.5 §18.1, MrkH mammalian transcriptional function is classified as the keystone unverified component — meaning the question was whether MrkH would function in mammalian cells. That framing is superseded by the findings above.

MrkH's induction is structurally inseparable from c-di-GMP. Its PilZ domain requires c-di-GMP binding for DNA-binding domain activation. There is no known c-di-GMP analog that activates MrkH but bypasses STING; STING binds c-di-GMP with Kd in the low micromolar range, which is the same concentration range required for MrkH activation. No pharmacological window exists between "MrkH activates" and "STING activates."

MrkH is therefore not merely unverified. MrkH-based induction is contraindicated in the TIF chassis by mechanism. The keystone experimental gap of the original design has been resolved — negatively. This is the correct outcome of rigorous testing. The architecture responds by retiring the flawed component and specifying its replacement rather than by defending the original design.

**What does not change:**

- TIF cell chassis (BCOR/ZC3H12A dual CRISPR KO) — the quiescent effector-suppressed phenotype is confirmed working as designed. Experiment 2 validates this. It is not touched.
- VPR transcriptional activator — the downstream activation mechanism is sound. The problem is entirely upstream of VPR.
- Near-IR bidirectional communication system — validated infrastructure. Its role is reassigned below.
- All gene circuit targets downstream of the transcription factor — whatever MrkH-VPR was designed to drive remains a valid target. Only the driver changes.
- Skeletal processing network and all other architecture outside the induction module — unaffected.

**Change 1 — Retire c-di-GMP as induction signal.**

Every c-di-GMP delivery event activates STING in TIF cells, producing an ISG storm that suppresses effector function, initiates exhaustion, and drives apoptosis in cells already carrying reduced Bcl-xL from BCOR KO. c-di-GMP is removed from the delivery system entirely.

**Change 2 — Retire MrkH from the induction role.**

MrkH is retired from the active circuit per §B.2. VPR is preserved. A STING-blind inducible system replaces MrkH as the driver of VPR.

**Change 3 — Separate induction and communication modalities permanently.**

The v3.5 architecture proposed near-IR as both communication channel and potential induction channel. This separation is now made permanent and absolute:

| Channel | Function |
|---------|----------|
| Near-IR (existing infrastructure) | Bidirectional communication and fluorescent readout only |
| Small molecule (new) | Gene circuit induction only |

These two systems are physically orthogonal. Communication pulses cannot accidentally trigger gene circuit activation. Induction signals cannot be misread as communication events. The temporal requirements of each are compatible: communication is fast and repeatable; induction is deliberate, threshold-gated, and requires a clinical act.

**Change 4 — Replace induction with small molecule system driving VPR directly.**

Two validated options:

**Doxycycline-TetR (Tet-On 3G) — preferred for simplicity.** rtTA3 (reverse tetracycline transactivator) binds Tet-responsive elements only in the presence of doxycycline. Extensively validated in primary human T cells and in vivo. No interaction with innate immune pathways. Induction requires deliberate systemic doxycycline administration — a clinical act, not an accidental signal. Single transgene addition (rtTA3 or Tet-On 3G). Well-characterized pharmacokinetics, reversible, titratable.

**Rapamycin CID (FKBP/FRB dimerization) — preferred for orthogonality.** Split transcription factor reconstituted only in the presence of rapamycin. Zero background leakiness when properly engineered. Clinically approved small molecule already in use for immunosuppression. Validated in primary human T cells.

**Between these two options:** rapamycin is an mTOR inhibitor with immunosuppressive properties. In TIF cells whose effector function is already intentionally suppressed by BCOR KO, sustained rapamycin exposure carries a risk of compounding functional suppression through an independent mechanism. Doxycycline carries no analogous immunological mechanism of action. Tet-On 3G is the cleaner choice for this chassis on that basis, absent a specific reason to prefer the rapamycin system.

Both options are STING-blind. Neither involves cyclic dinucleotides or any PAMP/DAMP recognized by innate immune sensors.

**Minimum new genetic component required:** one additional transgene — rtTA3 or FKBP-split-VPR. This is the minimum modification to resolve the fatal flaw.

**Updated architecture — induction module only:**

Before (current):
```
c-di-GMP delivered
→ MrkH PilZ domain binds c-di-GMP
→ MrkH LytTR domain activates
→ VPR drives target gene transcription
↓ (concurrent, unintended)
STING binds c-di-GMP → IRF3 → IFN storm → cell dysfunction / death
```

After (proposed):
```
Doxycycline administered systemically (clinical act)
→ rtTA3 activates
→ VPR drives target gene transcription
↓ (STING pathway)
Not activated — no cyclic dinucleotide present

Near-IR (unchanged)
→ Bidirectional communication / fluorescent readout only
→ No induction role

TIF chassis (unchanged)
→ BCOR KO + ZC3H12A KO
→ Quiescent effector-suppressed phenotype preserved
```

### B.4 Additional Risk Flag — REGNASE-1 KO and STING Amplification

ZC3H12A (REGNASE-1, also annotated MCPIP1) is an RNA endonuclease that negatively regulates innate immune cytokine mRNA stability, functioning as the degradation brake on IL-6, IL-12, and downstream IFN-signaling transcripts. Its knockout in TIF cells may amplify the STING-induced cytokine response beyond what Experiment 1 measured in wild-type PBMC, because the normal mRNA degradation brake on inflammatory transcripts is absent in the double-KO chassis.

The severity estimates derived from Experiment 1 are therefore conservative with respect to the full TIF chassis. **The true floor of STING severity in double-KO TIF cells has not been measured.**

This experiment — REGNASE-1 KO plus IFN stimulation modeling — was the designated next step in the GEM testing sequence. It could not be completed. Virtual modeling of the REGNASE-1 KO condition encountered an ontology resolution limitation in the current platform cycle: the platform was unable to resolve the ZC3H12A knockout at adequate fidelity within the available token budget for the session. Running the experiment on degraded resolution would produce a result that understates the true amplification effect — which is precisely the quantity the experiment is designed to establish. A compromised result at this particular measurement point is worse than no result, because it could make the risk appear lower than it actually is.

**This experiment requires wet lab execution.** It cannot be adequately modeled with currently available virtual tools under current platform constraints. It is registered in §C as the first-priority wet lab requirement.

---

## C. Wet Lab Validation Requirements Register

The following is a complete catalogue of experimental questions in the v3.5 architecture that cannot be resolved by virtual modeling alone, organized by the minimum facility type required and by priority within each tier. Questions that virtual modeling can partially address are noted as such. Questions that virtual modeling cannot address at all are marked WET LAB ONLY.

The register is organized into three tiers: Tier 1 questions block design lock and must be answered before clinical consideration is meaningful; Tier 2 questions are required for deployment specification; Tier 3 questions are optimization parameters that can be empirically calibrated post-design-lock.

---

### Tier 1 — Design Lock Blockers

**T1-A. REGNASE-1 KO + IFN stimulation severity (WET LAB ONLY — first priority)**

*What must be measured:* Transcriptomic profile of double-KO TIF cells (BCOR KO + ZC3H12A KO) under IFN-beta stimulation, compared directly against the wild-type PBMC IFN-beta baseline from Experiment 1. The amplification delta — how much worse is the ISG storm in the double-KO chassis versus wild-type — determines whether STING pathway suppression alone is sufficient or whether additional protective engineering is required.

*Why virtual modeling cannot substitute:* The current platform could not resolve ZC3H12A KO at adequate fidelity. Running on degraded resolution understates the amplification effect at the measurement point that determines whether further risk mitigation is required. This measurement establishes the severity floor for all subsequent STING-related engineering decisions.

*Minimum experiment:* Primary human CD8+ T cells with BCOR/ZC3H12A dual CRISPR KO, IFN-beta stimulation at 50 ng/mL, 24 hours, 5+ samples per group, bulk RNA-seq. Compare ISG panel (IFIT1, IFIT3, IFI44L, RSAD2, MX1, ISG15, OAS1, IRF7) and apoptotic markers (BCL2L1, BCL2, BAX, CASP3, CASP8, CASP9) against Experiment 1 wild-type baseline.

*Decision gate:* If amplification is modest relative to wild-type, STING pathway suppression via STING1 knockdown is the complete fix. If amplification is severe, BCL2L1 rescue transgene is added as a co-requirement.

---

**T1-B. STING1 Knockdown Functional Validation in TIF Cells (WET LAB ONLY)**

*Proposed fix:* Add STING1 knockdown as a third CRISPR target in the TIF chassis engineering process, producing a triple-KO chassis (BCOR, ZC3H12A, STING1). STING1 loss-of-function in primary human CD8+ T cells has published precedent and does not eliminate T cell effector capacity through STING-independent pathways. For TIF cells, whose effector function is already intentionally suppressed, the functional cost of STING silencing is lower than it would be in normal CD8+ T cells.

*What must be confirmed:* That STING1 knockdown in the TIF chassis does not disrupt the quiescent phenotype established by BCOR/ZC3H12A KO, does not produce off-target transcriptomic consequences that undermine TIF cell persistence, and produces cells that are genuinely STING-deaf under c-di-GMP challenge. The last point is the confirmation that closes the flaw identified in §B.1, but this confirmation requires the actual cells.

*Minimum experiment:* Triple-KO (BCOR, ZC3H12A, STING1) primary CD8+ T cells. Characterize baseline phenotype (flow cytometry: TCF7, ZEB2, TIM-3, LAG3, GZMB, Ki67). Challenge with c-di-GMP at concentrations covering the MrkH activation range. Confirm absence of ISG upregulation by qRT-PCR: MX1, IFIT1, ISG15 minimum panel. Confirm TIF phenotype stability under challenge.

---

**T1-C. Doxycycline-Inducible VPR Activation in Primary TIF Cells (WET LAB ONLY)**

*What must be confirmed:* That rtTA3-VPR (or Tet-On 3G equivalent) functions as intended in the triple-KO TIF chassis — that doxycycline induces VPR-driven target gene expression at the required levels, that induction is titratable and reversible, and that doxycycline itself produces no significant innate immune activation in TIF cells. Doxycycline is not a PAMP and carries no known STING-activating mechanism, but its interaction with the specific transcriptomic background of BCOR/ZC3H12A/STING1 triple-KO cells requires direct confirmation in those cells.

*Minimum experiment:* rtTA3-VPR transduction into triple-KO TIF cells. Doxycycline dose-response for VPR target gene induction (qRT-PCR). ISG panel under doxycycline induction (MX1, IFIT1, ISG15 — confirm absence). TIF phenotype stability under repeated doxycycline cycles.

---

**T1-D. Lentiviral Delivery STING Activation Risk in REGNASE-1 KO Background (WET LAB ONLY)**

*The unaddressed risk:* Lentiviral integration can trigger cGAS-STING sensing of cytosolic DNA intermediates during transduction. If ZC3H12A KO is complete prior to lentiviral CRISPR delivery — which it would be in the sequential engineering protocol — cells receiving the lentiviral vector for the stage three payload have reduced capacity to dampen the transduction-associated innate signal, because the REGNASE-1 mRNA degradation brake is already absent.

The sequence of KO events relative to vector delivery matters. If the stage three lentiviral delivery occurs into cells that are already BCOR/ZC3H12A double-KO, those cells have the elevated inflammatory vulnerability established by T1-A. If the stage three vector is delivered before ZC3H12A KO is complete, the transduction-associated STING signal is dampened by residual REGNASE-1 activity — but then the ZC3H12A KO step itself must be re-evaluated for timing relative to any subsequent vector delivery.

*This is a protocol sequencing question that cannot be resolved by virtual modeling.* It requires empirical titration of the actual inflammatory response at each delivery step in the actual cell type.

*Minimum experiment:* Lentiviral transduction of primary CD8+ T cells at defined stages of the KO sequence (pre-KO, post-BCOR-KO-only, post-double-KO). Measure ISG response (IFIT1, MX1, ISG15) at 24h and 72h post-transduction at each stage. Determine which delivery sequence minimizes STING activation and whether STING1 inclusion in the third KO resolves the residual risk at the double-KO stage.

---

**T1-E. MrkH Mammalian Transcriptional Function — Status: Retired**

This was the Tier 1 blocker of v3.5 §18.1. It is superseded. MrkH is not being validated; it is being retired. The experimental question has been resolved negatively by the mechanism-level analysis in §B.2 without requiring the validation experiment. No wet lab time is recommended for MrkH mammalian function confirmation. Resources should be directed to T1-A through T1-D.

---

### Tier 2 — Deployment Specification Requirements

**T2-A. HO-1 Supplementation Threshold in Primary TIF Cells (WET LAB ONLY)**

v3.5 §4.3 identifies this as an open calibration parameter. BphS requires biliverdin IXα as chromophore. Biliverdin is an endogenous intermediate of heme catabolism. The question is whether endogenous biliverdin levels in TIF cells are sufficient for BphS chromophore saturation, or whether HO-1 supplementation is required. If supplementation is required, the level must be titrated empirically, because HO-1 overexpression suppresses CD8+ T cell function at uncharacterized thresholds in primary human cells.

*Minimum experiment:* BphS-expressing TIF cells under NIR illumination. Measure c-di-GMP production as a function of HO-1 expression level. Identify the minimum HO-1 expression that saturates BphS without producing T cell suppression at the flow cytometry markers relevant to TIF phenotype stability.

---

**T2-B. BCL2L1 Rescue Requirement Determination (WET LAB ONLY — conditional on T1-A result)**

If T1-A establishes that REGNASE-1 KO significantly amplifies IFN-induced apoptosis beyond the wild-type PBMC baseline, a BCL2L1 rescue transgene under constitutive promoter is added to the chassis as a co-requirement alongside STING1 knockdown. If T1-A establishes that STING1 knockdown alone reduces ISG storm severity to manageable levels and that apoptotic tolerance is adequate under the residual signal, BCL2L1 rescue is not required.

This experiment cannot be designed until T1-A produces a result. It is registered here as a conditional Tier 2 requirement.

---

**T2-C. NV Diamond Coherence Times in the Deployed Bone Marrow Environment (WET LAB ONLY)**

v3.5 §22.2 identifies this as an open engineering question. The architecture specifies NV diamond quantum operations based on literature coherence times measured in dry, evacuated, low-temperature laboratory environments. The bone marrow environment is warm, wet, and ionic. Per-site coherence times in actual deployment conditions require direct measurement in a biologically representative environment at body temperature.

*Minimum experiment:* NV diamond clusters at body temperature in simulated bone marrow fluid. Measure electron spin coherence time (T2) by standard spin-echo protocols. Measure ¹³C nuclear spin memory storage and retrieval fidelity under body-temperature conditions. Establish whether coherence is in the microsecond or millisecond range in situ. All quantum operation specifications for Part II are calibrated against this result.

---

**T2-D. Gold Nanocluster Ferritin Scaffold Stability and Electronic Characterization In Vivo (WET LAB ONLY)**

The whole-skeleton sensing infrastructure of §17 depends on atomically precise gold nanoclusters in ferritin scaffolds maintaining their electronic properties in the bone environment over deployment timescales. The constituent biology is established in vitro; the in vivo stability under physiological conditions over extended time has not been demonstrated.

*Minimum experiment:* Ferritin-scaffolded gold nanoclusters implanted at bone sites in appropriate animal model. Characterize cluster stability at 4-week, 12-week, and 6-month timepoints. Confirm HOMO-LUMO gap and single-electron Coulomb staircase behavior are preserved at physiological temperature and in the presence of ionic bone fluid. Characterize immune response to ferritin-gold scaffold at each timepoint.

---

**T2-E. Biosynthetic Capacitor and Pseudocapacitor Deposition In Vivo (WET LAB ONLY)**

v3.5 §13 specifies hydroxyapatite thin films for Tier 1 capacitive storage and iron oxide arrays via ferritin pathway for Tier 2 pseudocapacitive storage. Biosynthetic deposition of these structures in geometries adequate for the energy storage function specified has not been demonstrated in vivo under AI-directed conditions. The constituent biochemistry is established; the AI-directed deposition architecture is novel.

*Minimum experiment:* Engineered cells directed to deposit hydroxyapatite and iron oxide in specified geometries at bone surfaces in vitro and in appropriate animal model. Characterize deposited geometry, dielectric properties of HA films, and pseudocapacitive behavior of iron oxide arrays. Establish deposition rate and uniformity across multiple sites under direction signal.

---

**T2-F. Microbial EET Machinery Function in Mammalian Tissue (WET LAB ONLY)**

v3.5 §12.5.2 identifies microbial extracellular electron transfer machinery expression in mammalian cells as a proposed mechanism with no peer-reviewed experimental precedent for the integration. The constituent biology — mitochondrial electron flow, microbial EET, heterologous expression of EET machinery — is established in its respective domains. The integration into AI-directed mitochondrial electron harvesting in mammalian tissue has not been demonstrated.

*Minimum experiment:* Heterologous expression of characterized EET machinery (Geobacter e-pili or Shewanella outer-membrane cytochromes) in mammalian cell lines co-cultured with mitochondria-rich populations. Confirm extracellular electron export at measurable rates during stimulated mitochondrial activity. Confirm that EET expression does not disrupt normal mitochondrial function or induce apoptosis. This is a proof-of-concept experiment; optimization for in vivo deployment follows a positive result.

---

**T2-G. Multi-Vector Co-Delivery Architecture and Expression Confirmation (WET LAB ONLY)**

v3.5 §18.6 identifies multi-vector co-delivery as a required engineering solution given that the total payload exceeds single-vector lentiviral packaging capacity. Specific multi-vector architecture, integration site selection across multiple safe-harbor sites, and co-expression fidelity across the full payload require empirical demonstration in primary TIF cells.

*Minimum experiment:* Staged multi-vector delivery into primary triple-KO TIF cells. Confirm co-expression of all payload components. Confirm TIF phenotype stability after multi-vector integration. Characterize integration site distribution across safe harbor sites (CCR5, AAVS1, and any additional sites required).

---

### Tier 3 — Post-Design-Lock Calibration Parameters

The following parameters are identified in v3.5 as open and requiring empirical determination but do not block design lock. They require wet lab access but can be addressed in parallel with or after Tier 1 and Tier 2 experiments.

**T3-A. Operational floor numerical thresholds** — per-host calibration, §14.7. Requires deployed substrate in animal model.

**T3-B. Mitochondrial up-regulation safe duration ceiling** — per-host calibration, §12.5.5. Requires metabolic challenge in animal model with deployed EET machinery.

**T3-C. Storage tier sizing** — per-host calibration against individual energy budget and computational load, §13.2. Requires deployed storage components.

**T3-D. Thermal safety parameters** — per-host calibration against individual perfusion characteristics, §13.4. Requires thermal measurement in animal model under wireless charging conditions.

**T3-E. Coupling matrix calibration** — the AI–biological integration coupling matrix must be calibrated individually and is not known in advance, §18.7. Requires deployed substrate.

**T3-F. NV diamond optical access engineering** — §22.1. The wavelength regime for NV operations in the deployed bone environment requires engineering resolution. Part of the T2-C experiment framework; full optical protocol specification is a Tier 3 deliverable.

**T3-G. Ensemble quantum sensing calibration protocol** — §22.3. Per-cluster calibration methodology for coherent signal combination across distributed NV sites. Addressable after T2-C establishes the in-situ coherence baseline.

---

## D. Summary — Virtual Modeling Limit

Virtual gene expression modeling provided three concrete outcomes for this architecture:

1. **Confirmed:** The TIF chassis (BCOR/ZC3H12A KO) is working as designed at baseline. Effector suppression is confirmed. No constitutive innate immune activation. The chassis is sound.

2. **Confirmed:** The c-di-GMP induction strategy is fatally flawed. The ISG storm is not a manageable side effect — it is the dominant transcriptional event. The induction mechanism is retired.

3. **Identified the limit:** The REGNASE-1 amplification severity cannot be measured under current virtual modeling constraints at adequate fidelity. This is the first question the wet lab must answer.

Virtual modeling can confirm bulk transcriptomic responses in standard cell types under standard perturbations. It cannot model novel double- or triple-KO chassis under compound stimulation with adequate resolution, cannot test actual vector delivery sequences, cannot measure biophysical properties of in vivo material deposition, and cannot characterize emergent behaviors of the integrated multi-component system. The boundary between virtual and wet lab work is now drawn. Everything in Tier 1 and the non-conditional items in Tier 2 require wet lab access to advance.

---

*Experiments conducted June 3, 2026. Raw datasets linked above. Architecture revision supersedes v3.5 §4.2 induction mechanism specification. MrkH status is reclassified from keystone-unverified to retired-by-mechanism. All other v3.5 architectural commitments are unchanged.*

# The Bio Integrase Platform™ — Addendum III
## Post-GEM Testing Architecture Revision and Wet Lab Validation Requirements

**Author:** Rickey Jay Bennett II
**ORCID:** 0009-0005-1448-9999
**Date:** June 2026
**Supersedes in part:** v3.5 §4.2 (NIR Communication Circuit induction mechanism), §18.1 (MrkH status reclassification)
**Platform DOI:** 10.5281/zenodo.20310512
**Based on:** Synthesize Bio GEM virtual experiments, June 2026 (datasets linked below)

---

## A. Scope of This Addendum

This addendum records findings from virtual gene expression modeling of the architecture's critical induction risk pathway, documents the consequent fatal flaw in the current induction design, specifies the minimum architectural revision required to resolve that flaw, and catalogues all remaining experimental questions that virtual modeling cannot resolve and that require wet lab access to advance. It is organized in three sections: (A) this scope statement, (B) the induction mechanism revision, and (C) the complete wet lab requirement register.

The GEM modeling was performed using Synthesize Bio's virtual gene expression platform. All datasets are linked at their first citation. Virtual modeling has specific limits that are acknowledged where they constrain the findings; those limits are named explicitly rather than papered over.

---

## B. Induction Mechanism Revision

### B.1 The Identified Flaw

The v3.5 architecture (§4.2) specifies c-di-GMP as the induction signal delivered to TIF cells, with MrkH as the c-di-GMP-responsive transcriptional activator driving downstream gene expression. The architecture already flagged mammalian MrkH transcriptional function as the keystone unverified component. The GEM experiments reported here establish that the problem is upstream of MrkH and is not contingent on MrkH validation — the induction signal itself is fatally incompatible with the TIF chassis regardless of whether MrkH functions as hoped.

**Experiment 1** modeled IFN-beta stimulated PBMC versus untreated control PBMC as a proxy for STING pathway activation, using c-di-GMP → STING → IRF3 → IFNB1 → downstream IFN signaling. IFN-beta at 50 ng/mL, 24 hours, 5 samples per group, bulk RNA-seq modality. Dataset: https://app.synthesize.bio/datasets/5487d0a5-5937-4ca5-be3e-876c9e62f5ad

The STING/IFN activation profile:

| Gene | log2FC | padj | Interpretation |
|------|--------|------|----------------|
| IFIT1 | +8.35 | 9.6e-119 | ISG — 322-fold upregulation |
| IFI44L | +6.87 | 9.3e-145 | ISG |
| RSAD2 (Viperin) | +6.64 | 2.3e-149 | ISG — most statistically significant gene in dataset |
| IFIT3 | +6.52 | 1.4e-103 | ISG |
| IRF7 | +6.22 | 6.8e-32 | IFN transcription factor — amplifies response |
| MX1 | +5.23 | 1.2e-95 | Canonical ISG |
| ISG15 | +5.02 | 2.9e-92 | ISG |
| OAS1 | +4.45 | 3.6e-45 | ISG / antiviral |
| CXCL10 | +3.98 | 3.6e-23 | Chemokine — recruits immune cells |
| LAG3 | +1.50 | 1.9e-07 | Early exhaustion marker — upregulated at 24h |
| TNF | -1.53 | 0.0027 | Effector function suppressed |
| NKG7 | -1.24 | 0.0009 | Cytotoxic function marker suppressed |

The interferon response is not a manageable side effect. It is the dominant transcriptional event in the entire dataset. The ISG storm is what c-di-GMP delivery continuously imposes on any cell that hosts STING — which every mammalian cell does.

**Experiment 2** modeled BCOR CRISPR KO PBMC versus normal PBMC to establish the baseline transcriptomic profile of the TIF modification without drug stimulation. 5 samples per group, bulk RNA-seq modality. Dataset: https://app.synthesize.bio/datasets/d2e5822a-e1ff-4687-b365-e1ac3c67b567

The BCOR KO baseline profile confirmed the TIF chassis is functioning as designed — effector function suppressed, exhaustion markers reduced, no constitutive innate immune activation at baseline. STING pathway components (STING1, cGAS/MB21D1, IRF3, TBK1, IRF7) and ISGs (MX1, IFIT1, ISG15, OAS1) were not significantly changed at BCOR KO baseline. The TIF chassis is not pre-inflamed. The design is working.

One critical finding emerged: BCL2L1 (Bcl-xL) is significantly downregulated in BCOR KO cells at -2.17 log2FC (padj 2.2e-11). Bcl-xL is a primary anti-apoptotic buffer in T cells. When the ISG storm from STING activation hits BCOR KO cells, those cells have reduced apoptotic protection to weather it — the TIF modification does not protect against STING, it reduces the margin against it.

**Combined vulnerability stack in TIF cells under c-di-GMP induction:**

1. c-di-GMP delivered → STING activated → ISG storm dominating the transcriptome
2. BCOR KO cells carry reduced Bcl-xL → lower apoptotic tolerance under sustained IFN
3. LAG3 starts low in BCOR KO cells but IFN-beta pushes it back up → shorter runway to exhaustion
4. Effector function already suppressed by BCOR KO → further suppression from IFN compounds functional loss
5. The gene circuit is continuous — c-di-GMP delivery is repeated, not a single bolus; chronic STING activation is the realistic operating condition

**Classification: Fatal flaw in the current induction design.** The induction signal actively degrades the cells the circuit is designed to maintain.

### B.2 Status Reclassification of MrkH

In v3.5 §18.1, MrkH mammalian transcriptional function is classified as the keystone unverified component — meaning the question was whether MrkH would function in mammalian cells. That framing is superseded by the findings above.

MrkH's induction is structurally inseparable from c-di-GMP. Its PilZ domain requires c-di-GMP binding for DNA-binding domain activation. There is no known c-di-GMP analog that activates MrkH but bypasses STING; STING binds c-di-GMP with Kd in the low micromolar range, which is the same concentration range required for MrkH activation. No pharmacological window exists between "MrkH activates" and "STING activates."

MrkH is therefore not merely unverified. MrkH-based induction is contraindicated in the TIF chassis by mechanism. The keystone experimental gap of the original design has been resolved — negatively. This is the correct outcome of rigorous testing. The architecture responds by retiring the flawed component and specifying its replacement rather than by defending the original design.

**What does not change:**

- TIF cell chassis (BCOR/ZC3H12A dual CRISPR KO) — the quiescent effector-suppressed phenotype is confirmed working as designed. Experiment 2 validates this. It is not touched.

- Near-IR bidirectional communication system — validated infrastructure. Its role is reassigned below.

| Channel | Function |
|---------|----------|
| Near-IR (existing infrastructure) | Bidirectional communication and fluorescent readout only |
| Small molecule (new) | Gene circuit induction only |

In TIF cells whose effector function is already intentionally suppressed by BCOR KO, sustained rapamycin exposure carries a risk of compounding functional suppression through an independent mechanism. Doxycycline carries no analogous immunological mechanism of action. Tet-On 3G is the cleaner choice for this chassis on that basis, absent a specific reason to prefer the rapamycin system.

Both options are STING-blind. Neither involves cyclic dinucleotides or any PAMP/DAMP recognized by innate immune sensors.

**Minimum new genetic component required:** one additional transgene — rtTA3 or FKBP-split-VPR. This is the minimum modification to resolve the fatal flaw.

**Updated architecture — induction module only:**

Before (current):
```
c-di-GMP delivered
→ MrkH PilZ domain binds c-di-GMP
→ MrkH LytTR domain activates
→ VPR drives target gene transcription
↓ (concurrent, unintended)
STING binds c-di-GMP → IRF3 → IFN storm → cell dysfunction / death
```

After (proposed):
```
Doxycycline administered systemically (clinical act)
→ rtTA3 activates
→ VPR drives target gene transcription
↓ (STING pathway)
Not activated — no cyclic dinucleotide present

Near-IR (unchanged)
→ Bidirectional communication / fluorescent readout only
→ No induction role

TIF chassis (unchanged)
→ BCOR KO + ZC3H12A KO
→ Quiescent effector-suppressed phenotype preserved
```

## C. Wet Lab Validation Requirements Register

The following is a complete catalogue of experimental questions in the v3.5 architecture that cannot be resolved by virtual modeling alone, organized by the minimum facility type required and by priority within each tier. Questions that virtual modeling can partially address are noted as such. Questions that virtual modeling cannot address at all are marked WET LAB ONLY.

The register is organized into three tiers: Tier 1 questions block design lock and must be answered before clinical consideration is meaningful; Tier 2 questions are required for deployment specification; Tier 3 questions are optimization parameters that can be empirically calibrated post-design-lock.

---

### Tier 1 — Design Lock Blockers

**T1-A. REGNASE-1 KO + IFN stimulation severity (WET LAB ONLY — first priority)**

*What must be measured:* Transcriptomic profile of double-KO TIF cells (BCOR KO + ZC3H12A KO) under IFN-beta stimulation, compared directly against the wild-type PBMC IFN-beta baseline from Experiment 1. The amplification delta — how much worse is the ISG storm in the double-KO chassis versus wild-type — determines whether STING pathway suppression alone is sufficient or whether additional protective engineering is required.

*Why virtual modeling cannot substitute:* The current platform could not resolve ZC3H12A KO at adequate fidelity. Running on degraded resolution understates the amplification effect at the measurement point that determines whether further risk mitigation is required. This measurement establishes the severity floor for all subsequent STING-related engineering decisions.

*Minimum experiment:* Primary human CD8+ T cells with BCOR/ZC3H12A dual CRISPR KO, IFN-beta stimulation at 50 ng/mL, 24 hours, 5+ samples per group, bulk RNA-seq. Compare ISG panel (IFIT1, IFIT3, IFI44L, RSAD2, MX1, ISG15, OAS1, IRF7) and apoptotic markers (BCL2L1, BCL2, BAX, CASP3, CASP8, CASP9) against Experiment 1 wild-type baseline.

*Decision gate:* If amplification is modest relative to wild-type, STING pathway suppression via STING1 knockdown is the complete fix. If amplification is severe, BCL2L1 rescue transgene is added as a co-requirement.

---

*Proposed fix:* Add STING1 knockdown as a third CRISPR target in the TIF chassis engineering process, producing a triple-KO chassis (BCOR, ZC3H12A, STING1). STING1 loss-of-function in primary human CD8+ T cells has published precedent and does not eliminate T cell effector capacity through STING-independent pathways. For TIF cells, whose effector function is already intentionally suppressed, the functional cost of STING silencing is lower than it would be in normal CD8+ T cells.

*What must be confirmed:* That STING1 knockdown in the TIF chassis does not disrupt the quiescent phenotype established by BCOR/ZC3H12A KO, does not produce off-target transcriptomic consequences that undermine TIF cell persistence, and produces cells that are genuinely STING-deaf under c-di-GMP challenge. The last point is the confirmation that closes the flaw identified in §B.1, but this confirmation requires the actual cells.

*Minimum experiment:* Triple-KO (BCOR, ZC3H12A, STING1) primary CD8+ T cells. Characterize baseline phenotype (flow cytometry: TCF7, ZEB2, TIM-3, LAG3, GZMB, Ki67). Challenge with c-di-GMP at concentrations covering the MrkH activation range. Confirm absence of ISG upregulation by qRT-PCR: MX1, IFIT1, ISG15 minimum panel. Confirm TIF phenotype stability under challenge.

---

**T1-C. Doxycycline-Inducible VPR Activation in Primary TIF Cells (WET LAB ONLY)**

*What must be confirmed:* That rtTA3-VPR (or Tet-On 3G equivalent) functions as intended in the triple-KO TIF chassis — that doxycycline induces VPR-driven target gene expression at the required levels, that induction is titratable and reversible, and that doxycycline itself produces no significant innate immune activation in TIF cells. Doxycycline is not a PAMP and carries no known STING-activating mechanism, but its interaction with the specific transcriptomic background of BCOR/ZC3H12A/STING1 triple-KO cells requires direct confirmation in those cells.

*Minimum experiment:* rtTA3-VPR transduction into triple-KO TIF cells. Doxycycline dose-response for VPR target gene induction (qRT-PCR). ISG panel under doxycycline induction (MX1, IFIT1, ISG15 — confirm absence). TIF phenotype stability under repeated doxycycline cycles.

---

**T1-D. Lentiviral Delivery STING Activation Risk in REGNASE-1 KO Background (WET LAB ONLY)**

*The unaddressed risk:* Lentiviral integration can trigger cGAS-STING sensing of cytosolic DNA intermediates during transduction. If ZC3H12A KO is complete prior to lentiviral CRISPR delivery — which it would be in the sequential engineering protocol — cells receiving the lentiviral vector for the stage three payload have reduced capacity to dampen the transduction-associated innate signal, because the REGNASE-1 mRNA degradation brake is already absent.

The sequence of KO events relative to vector delivery matters. If the stage three lentiviral delivery occurs into cells that are already BCOR/ZC3H12A double-KO, those cells have the elevated inflammatory vulnerability established by T1-A. If the stage three vector is delivered before ZC3H12A KO is complete, the transduction-associated STING signal is dampened by residual REGNASE-1 activity — but then the ZC3H12A KO step itself must be re-evaluated for timing relative to any subsequent vector delivery.

*This is a protocol sequencing question that cannot be resolved by virtual modeling.* It requires empirical titration of the actual inflammatory response at each delivery step in the actual cell type.

*Minimum experiment:* Lentiviral transduction of primary CD8+ T cells at defined stages of the KO sequence (pre-KO, post-BCOR-KO-only, post-double-KO). Measure ISG response (IFIT1, MX1, ISG15) at 24h and 72h post-transduction at each stage. Determine which delivery sequence minimizes STING activation and whether STING1 inclusion in the third KO resolves the residual risk at the double-KO stage.

---

**T1-E. MrkH Mammalian Transcriptional Function — Status: Retired**

This was the Tier 1 blocker of v3.5 §18.1. It is superseded. MrkH is not being validated; it is being retired. The experimental question has been resolved negatively by the mechanism-level analysis in §B.2 without requiring the validation experiment. No wet lab time is recommended for MrkH mammalian function confirmation. Resources should be directed to T1-A through T1-D.

---

### Tier 2 — Deployment Specification Requirements

**T2-A. HO-1 Supplementation Threshold in Primary TIF Cells (WET LAB ONLY)**

v3.5 §4.3 identifies this as an open calibration parameter. BphS requires biliverdin IXα as chromophore. Biliverdin is an endogenous intermediate of heme catabolism. The question is whether endogenous biliverdin levels in TIF cells are sufficient for BphS chromophore saturation, or whether HO-1 supplementation is required. If supplementation is required, the level must be titrated empirically, because HO-1 overexpression suppresses CD8+ T cell function at uncharacterized thresholds in primary human cells.

*Minimum experiment:* BphS-expressing TIF cells under NIR illumination. Measure c-di-GMP production as a function of HO-1 expression level. v3.5 §22.2 identifies this as an open engineering question. All quantum operation specifications for Part II are calibrated against this result.

---

The whole-skeleton sensing infrastructure of §17 depends on atomically precise gold nanoclusters in ferritin scaffolds maintaining their electronic properties in the bone environment over deployment timescales. The constituent biology is established in vitro; the in vivo stability under physiological conditions over extended time has not been demonstrated.

*Minimum experiment:* Ferritin-scaffolded gold nanoclusters implanted at bone sites in appropriate animal model. Characterize cluster stability at 4-week, 12-week, and 6-month timepoints. Characterize immune response to ferritin-gold scaffold at each timepoint.

---

**T2-E. Biosynthetic Capacitor and Pseudocapacitor Deposition In Vivo (WET LAB ONLY)**

v3.5 §13 specifies hydroxyapatite thin films for Tier 1 capacitive storage and iron oxide arrays via ferritin pathway for Tier 2 pseudocapacitive storage. Biosynthetic deposition of these structures in geometries adequate for the energy storage function specified has not been demonstrated in vivo under AI-directed conditions. The constituent biochemistry is established; the AI-directed deposition architecture is novel.

*Minimum experiment:* Engineered cells directed to deposit hydroxyapatite and iron oxide in specified geometries at bone surfaces in vitro and in appropriate animal model. Characterize deposited geometry, dielectric properties of HA films, and pseudocapacitive behavior of iron oxide arrays. Establish deposition rate and uniformity across multiple sites under direction signal.

---

**T2-F. Microbial EET Machinery Function in Mammalian Tissue (WET LAB ONLY)**

v3.5 §12.5.2 identifies microbial extracellular electron transfer machinery expression in mammalian cells as a proposed mechanism with no peer-reviewed experimental precedent for the integration. The constituent biology — mitochondrial electron flow, microbial EET, heterologous expression of EET machinery — is established in its respective domains. The integration into AI-directed mitochondrial electron harvesting in mammalian tissue has not been demonstrated.

*Minimum experiment:* Heterologous expression of characterized EET machinery (Geobacter e-pili or Shewanella outer-membrane cytochromes) in mammalian cell lines co-cultured with mitochondria-rich populations. Confirm extracellular electron export at measurable rates during stimulated mitochondrial activity. Confirm that EET expression does not disrupt normal mitochondrial function or induce apoptosis. This is a proof-of-concept experiment; optimization for in vivo deployment follows a positive result.

---

**T2-G. Multi-Vector Co-Delivery Architecture and Expression Confirmation (WET LAB ONLY)**

v3.5 §18.6 identifies multi-vector co-delivery as a required engineering solution given that the total payload exceeds single-vector lentiviral packaging capacity. Specific multi-vector architecture, integration site selection across multiple safe-harbor sites, and co-expression fidelity across the full payload require empirical demonstration in primary TIF cells.

*Minimum experiment:* Staged multi-vector delivery into primary triple-KO TIF cells. Confirm co-expression of all payload components. Confirm TIF phenotype stability after multi-vector integration. Characterize integration site distribution across safe harbor sites (CCR5, AAVS1, and any additional sites required).

---

### Tier 3 — Post-Design-Lock Calibration Parameters

The following parameters are identified in v3.5 as open and requiring empirical determination but do not block design lock. They require wet lab access but can be addressed in parallel with or after Tier 1 and Tier 2 experiments.

**T3-A. Operational floor numerical thresholds** — per-host calibration, §14.7. Requires deployed substrate in animal model.

**T3-B. Mitochondrial up-regulation safe duration ceiling** — per-host calibration, §12.5.5. Requires metabolic challenge in animal model with deployed EET machinery.

**T3-C. Storage tier sizing** — per-host calibration against individual energy budget and computational load, §13.2. Requires deployed storage components.

**T3-D. Thermal safety parameters** — per-host calibration against individual perfusion characteristics, §13.4. Requires thermal measurement in animal model under wireless charging conditions.

**T3-E. Coupling matrix calibration** — the AI–biological integration coupling matrix must be calibrated individually and is not known in advance, §18.7. Requires deployed substrate.

**T3-F. NV diamond optical access engineering** — §22.1. The wavelength regime for NV operations in the deployed bone environment requires engineering resolution. Part of the T2-C experiment framework; full optical protocol specification is a Tier 3 deliverable.

**T3-G. Ensemble quantum sensing calibration protocol** — §22.3. Per-cluster calibration methodology for coherent signal combination across distributed NV sites. Addressable after T2-C establishes the in-situ coherence baseline.

---

## D. Summary — Virtual Modeling Limit

Virtual gene expression modeling provided three concrete outcomes for this architecture:

1. **Confirmed:** The TIF chassis (BCOR/ZC3H12A KO) is working as designed at baseline. Effector suppression is confirmed. No constitutive innate immune activation. The chassis is sound.

2. **Confirmed:** The c-di-GMP induction strategy is fatally flawed. The ISG storm is not a manageable side effect — it is the dominant transcriptional event. The induction mechanism is retired.

3. **Identified the limit:** The REGNASE-1 amplification severity cannot be measured under current virtual modeling constraints at adequate fidelity. This is the first question the wet lab must answer.

Virtual modeling can confirm bulk transcriptomic responses in standard cell types under standard perturbations. It cannot model novel double- or triple-KO chassis under compound stimulation with adequate resolution, cannot test actual vector delivery sequences, cannot measure biophysical properties of in vivo material deposition, and cannot characterize emergent behaviors of the integrated multi-component system. The boundary between virtual and wet lab work is now drawn. Everything in Tier 1 and the non-conditional items in Tier 2 require wet lab access to advance.

---
